liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Crazy Fingers** (2 reviews): Crazy Fingers gets a long jam that drifts into space; The Crazy Fingers into Let It Grow transition is singled out as really nice [20][26]
- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Let It Grow as great; Let It Grow also gets a long, spacey jam in the first set [18][20]
- **High Time** (2 reviews): The second-set High Time is in the 1976 style, with Donna's harmonies a big appeal; High Time is also singled out as a highlight [20][26]
- **Stella Blue** (2 reviews): Reviewer recommends Stella Blue as a highlight; Stella Blue moves through Keith's chords in a starry, dark mood [19][24]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): Reviewer counts this Mississippi Half-Step among their favorites; the sound is thick [24]
- **Saint Stephen** (1 review): Saint Stephen contains slick, mellow guitar licks [19]

## The recordings

- **gd76-07-13.sbd.ashley-bertha.9978.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 157 min; rated 3.38/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: The soundboard is fairly clear, though the Dancin' in the Streets bounces a bit; Bertha remaster has strong bass but considerable tape hiss; the opening Half Step sounds muddy until Big River [16][27]
- **gd1976-07-13.157454.mtx.motb.0199.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 157 min [2]
- **gd76-07-13.sbd.vernon.18480.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 149 min; rated 4.57/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: The matrix has noticeably less hiss and a fuller sound than the other source [26]
- **gd76-07-13.menke.minches.18427.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 2.8/5 by 5 [4]. Said about its sound: The audience tape is somewhat trebly and echoey; The audience recording runs about a half step sharp and slightly fast, from a deck speed mismatch; The audience version's sound is weak; reviewer advises seeking the board instead [19][21][23]
- **gd1976-07-13.150753.sbd.miller.fixed.flac2448**: soundboard; 18 songs; 162 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: This version fixes the Crazy Fingers dropout, and pitch is improved though imperfect [5]
- **gd1976-07-13.150753.sbd.koda.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 18 songs; 162 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]. Said about its sound: Pitch is improved over earlier versions but still not perfect [6]

## Around the show

- All three sources lack the start of Mississippi Half-Step; the Menke tape flips mid-Dancin' in the Streets [2]
- The soundboard source lacks Music Never Stopped and has a 40-second gap in the Saint Stephen jam [2]
- Reviewer calls this show okay but unremarkable; the July 18 Orpheum show's second set is probably 1976's best [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-07-13.sbd.ashley-bertha.9978.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Jay Ashley (Bertha) remaster of a multi-generation reel source [1]
- **gd1976-07-13.157454.mtx.motb.0199.flac16**: taped by AUD Source #1 Taped By: Bob Menke AUD Source #2 Taped By: Reinhart Hohlwein; transferred by Transfer By: Bob Menke Matrix & Mastering By: Derek McCabe; source: Analog Soundboard Source: gd76-07-13.18480.sbd.vernon.flac16 Analog Audience Source #1: ECM 280's 152 - center balcony Medium Stock Brands #1: MAC = TDK SA… [2]. Also: Matrix of three sources: a soundboard, Menke's audience tape, and a third; the soundboard was very hissy and noise-reduced [2]
- **gd76-07-13.sbd.vernon.18480.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd76-07-13.menke.minches.18427.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by David Minches; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-270s> Sony TC-152 from front of balcony [4]
- **gd1976-07-13.150753.sbd.miller.fixed.flac2448**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  October 25, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette (Maxell UD) [5]. Also: Sony ECM-270 to cassette master to DAT; cassettes from Dennis Koda, patch source from Bob Menke [5]
- **gd1976-07-13.150753.sbd.koda.miller.flac2496**: taped by Dennis Koda; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette (Maxell UD) [6]. Also: Charlie Miller handled transfers and mastering from Sony ECM-270 to cassette master to DAT; cassettes from Dennis Koda [6]
